Haworth furanose ring (ring O at top) with anomeric C2 on the left ($\text{HOH}_2\text{C}$ up, $\text{HO}$ down), C3 at bottom-left ($\text{OH}$ up, $\text{H}$ down), C4 at bottom-right ($\text{H}$ up, $\text{OH}$ down), and C5 on the right ($\text{H}$ up, $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ down)
questions.explanationEn:
First construct the standard Haworth projection of $\alpha$-D-($-$)-fructofuranose from D-($-$)-fructose (C5 on left, C2 on right, ring O at top):
- C5 (left): $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ UP, $-\text{H}$ DOWN (D-sugar).
- C4 (bottom-left): $-\text{OH}$ was on the right in Fischer $\implies$ DOWN ($-\text{H}$ UP).
- C3 (bottom-right): $-\text{OH}$ was on the left in Fischer $\implies$ UP ($-\text{H}$ DOWN).
- C2 (right): for the $\alpha$-anomer, the anomeric $-\text{OH}$ is trans to the C5 $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group $\implies$ $-\text{OH}$ DOWN, $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ UP (which is option B).
Now, **$\alpha$-L-($+$)-fructofuranose** is the exact **enantiomer (mirror image)** of $\alpha$-D-($-$)-fructofuranose. Reflecting option (B) across a vertical mirror plane places C2 on the left ($\text{HOH}_2\text{C}$ up, $\text{HO}$ down), C3 at bottom-left ($\text{OH}$ up, $\text{H}$ down), C4 at bottom-right ($\text{H}$ up, $\text{OH}$ down), and C5 on the right ($\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ up, $\text{H}$ down). This matches option (A) exactly.

questions.questionTextEn:
The major products **X** and **Y** in the following reaction sequence are:
Starting material: (2-methoxy-6-methylphenyl)(pyrrolidin-1-yl)methanone (an $N,N$-tetramethylene 2-methoxy-6-methylbenzamide).
Step 1: 1. $\text{Na}$, $\text{NH}_3$ (liquid), $\text{THF}$; 2. allyl bromide ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br}$) $\longrightarrow$ **X**.
Step 2: 1. aqueous $\text{HCl}$; 2. 1,2-dichlorobenzene, reflux $\longrightarrow$ **Y**. [Diagram required - Q.42]
optionsEn: **X** = 1-allyl-2-methoxy-6-methyl-1-(pyrrolidine-1-carbonyl)cyclohexa-2,5-diene (Birch reductive alkylation ipso to the amide); **Y** = 4-allyl-4-methyl-2-(pyrrolidine-1-carbonyl)cyclohex-2-en-1-one (formed via enol ether hydrolysis and Cope rearrangement)
questions.explanationEn:
Step 1 is a **Birch reductive alkylation** of an electron-deficient benzamide derivative. The electron-withdrawing amide carbonyl directs Birch reduction to produce a stabilized carbanion **ipso** to the amide group (with the two double bonds of the cyclohexa-2,5-diene located at C2=C3 bearing the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group and C5=C6 bearing the $-\text{CH}_3$ group). Trapping this ipso carbanion with allyl bromide gives the 1-allyl-cyclohexa-2,5-diene **X**.
In Step 2, aqueous $\text{HCl}$ hydrolyzes the methyl enol ether ($\text{C=C-OMe}$) to a $\beta,\gamma$-unsaturated cyclohexenone while leaving the tertiary amide intact (ruling out C). Upon refluxing in 1,2-dichlorobenzene ($\sim 180\ ^\circ\text{C}$), the 1,5-diene system undergoes a thermal **[3,3]-sigmatropic Cope rearrangement**, migrating the allyl group from the $\alpha$-carbon (C2) to the methyl-bearing C4 position and shifting the double bond into conjugation with both carbonyls to yield the conjugated enone **Y** (4-allyl-4-methyl-2-(pyrrolidine-1-carbonyl)cyclohex-2-en-1-one). Thus, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
The major products **E** and **F** in the following reaction sequence are:
Starting material: piperonal (benzo[$d$][1,3]dioxole-5-carbaldehyde).
Step 1: (3-bromopropyl)triphenylphosphonium bromide ($[\text{Ph}_3\text{P}^+\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}]\text{Br}^-$), $\text{NaH}$ ($2\text{ equiv.}$), $\text{THF}$ $\longrightarrow$ **E**.
Step 2: 1. $m$-CPBA, $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$; 2. $\text{BF}_3\cdot\text{OEt}_2$ $\longrightarrow$ **F**. [Diagram required - Q.43]
questions.explanationEn:
Step 1 uses **2 equivalents of $\text{NaH}$** with (3-bromopropyl)triphenylphosphonium bromide: the first equivalent generates the phosphorus ylide, which undergoes intramolecular $S_N2$ cyclization (displacing $\text{Br}^-$) to form cyclopropyltriphenylphosphonium bromide; the second equivalent of $\text{NaH}$ deprotonates it to form the cyclopropylidene ylide. Wittig reaction with piperonal then yields the alkylidenecyclopropane **E**, 5-(cyclopropylidenemethyl)benzo[$d$][1,3]dioxole.
Step 2: Epoxidation of **E** with $m$-CPBA gives an oxaspiropentane intermediate. Upon treatment with the Lewis acid $\text{BF}_3\cdot\text{OEt}_2$, the epoxide opens at the **benzylic carbon** (generating a stabilized benzylic carbocation adjacent to the electron-rich benzodioxole ring), followed by a stereospecific **1,2-alkyl shift (ring expansion)** of a cyclopropane C-C bond to relieve ring strain and form a cyclobutanone with the aryl ring attached at C2 ($\alpha$ to the carbonyl), namely 2-(benzo[$d$][1,3]dioxol-5-yl)cyclobutan-1-one (**F**). Therefore, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
$\psi_1$, $\psi_2$, $\psi_3$, and $\psi_4$ are four Hückel molecular orbitals of benzene with orbital energies $E_1$, $E_2$, $E_3$, and $E_4$, respectively.
$\psi_1 = \frac{1}{2}(\phi_{\text{B}} + \phi_{\text{C}} - \phi_{\text{E}} - \phi_{\text{F}})$
$\psi_2 = 6^{-1/2}(\phi_{\text{A}} - \phi_{\text{B}} + \phi_{\text{C}} - \phi_{\text{D}} + \phi_{\text{E}} - \phi_{\text{F}})$
$\psi_3 = 6^{-1/2}(\phi_{\text{A}} + \phi_{\text{B}} + \phi_{\text{C}} + \phi_{\text{D}} + \phi_{\text{E}} + \phi_{\text{F}})$
$\psi_4 = 12^{-1/2}(2\phi_{\text{A}} + \phi_{\text{B}} - \phi_{\text{C}} - 2\phi_{\text{D}} - \phi_{\text{E}} + \phi_{\text{F}})$
The correct order of the orbital energies is
(The six carbon atoms of benzene are denoted by A to F and $\phi_J$ is the $2p_z$ orbital of $J^{\text{th}}$ carbon of benzene.)
questions.explanationEn:
In Hückel MO theory for benzene, orbital energy increases with the number of nodal planes (equivalently, evaluate $E = \alpha + \frac{2\sum_{\text{adj}} c_i c_j}{\sum c_i^2}\beta$ with $\beta < 0$):
- $\psi_3$: all 6 coefficients have the same sign ($+$) $\implies$ **0 nodal planes**, $E_3 = \alpha + 2\beta$ (lowest energy).
- $\psi_1$: signs around the ring are $(0, +, +, 0, -, -)$ $\implies$ **1 nodal plane** (through A and D), $E_1 = \alpha + \beta$.
- $\psi_4$: signs around the ring are $(+2, +1, -1, -2, -1, +1)$ $\implies$ **1 nodal plane** (between B-C and E-F), $E_4 = \alpha + \frac{2(2 - 1 + 2 + 2 - 1 + 2)}{12}\beta = \alpha + \beta$. Thus $E_1 = E_4$ (degenerate HOMO pair).
- $\psi_2$: signs alternate $(+, -, +, -, +, -)$ $\implies$ **3 nodal planes**, $E_2 = \alpha - 2\beta$ (highest energy).
Since $\beta < 0$, the energy order is $E_3 < E_1 = E_4 < E_2$, option (C).

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following six vibrational modes: symmetric stretching of $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{O-H}$ symmetric stretching of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, stretching of $\text{HCl}$, stretching of $\text{H}_2$, $\text{N-H}$ symmetric stretching of $\text{NH}_3$, and bending of $\text{CO}_2$.
Among these modes, if $k$ number of modes are IR active but Raman inactive, $l$ number of modes are IR inactive but Raman active, and $m$ number of modes are both IR and Raman active, $k$, $l$, and $m$, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn:
A vibrational mode is IR active if it changes the dipole moment and Raman active if it changes the polarizability. For centrosymmetric molecules ($\text{CO}_2$, $\text{H}_2$), the rule of mutual exclusion applies:
1. Symmetric stretching of $\text{CO}_2$ ($\Sigma_g^+$): **IR inactive, Raman active**.
2. $\text{O-H}$ symmetric stretching of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($C_{2v}$, $A_1$): **both IR and Raman active**.
3. Stretching of $\text{HCl}$ ($C_{\infty v}$): **both IR and Raman active**.
4. Stretching of $\text{H}_2$ ($D_{\infty h}$, $\Sigma_g^+$): **IR inactive, Raman active**.
5. $\text{N-H}$ symmetric stretching of $\text{NH}_3$ ($C_{3v}$, $A_1$): **both IR and Raman active**.
6. Bending of $\text{CO}_2$ ($\Pi_u$): **IR active, Raman inactive**.
Counting: $k$ (IR only) $= 1$, $l$ (Raman only) $= 2$, and $m$ (both IR and Raman) $= 3$. Thus, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
The correct statement for a thermally initiated radical polymerization in a solution is:
(Assume: Steady-state and equal reactivity of the propagating radicals, termination reactions are only by combination, and no chain transfer reaction. Given: $R_p =$ rate of polymerization, $\text{DP} =$ degree of polymerization, $[\text{I}] =$ initiator concentration, and $[\text{M}] =$ monomer concentration.)
optionsEn: with increase in $[\text{I}]$, both $R_p$ and $\text{DP}$ increase.
with increase in $[\text{M}]$, both $R_p$ and $\text{DP}$ increase.
$R_p$ decreases with increase in $[\text{I}]$ but $\text{DP}$ increases with increase in $[\text{M}]$.
$\text{DP}$ increases with increase in $[\text{I}]$ and $\text{DP}$ decreases with increase in $[\text{M}]$.
questions.explanationEn:
Under the steady-state approximation for free-radical polymerization with termination solely by combination and no chain transfer:
- Rate of polymerization: $R_p = k_p [\text{M}] \left(\frac{f k_d [\text{I}]}{k_t}\right)^{1/2} \propto [\text{M}][\text{I}]^{1/2}$.
- Kinetic chain length: $\nu = \frac{R_p}{R_i} = \frac{k_p [\text{M}]}{2 (f k_d k_t [\text{I}])^{1/2}}$, and for termination by combination, $\text{DP} = 2\nu = \frac{k_p [\text{M}]}{(f k_d k_t [\text{I}])^{1/2}} \propto \frac{[\text{M}]}{[\text{I}]^{1/2}}$.
From these expressions: increasing $[\text{I}]$ increases $R_p$ but decreases $\text{DP}$, whereas increasing $[\text{M}]$ increases **both** $R_p$ and $\text{DP}$ linearly. Therefore, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
If $q_t$ and $Q_{t,m}$ are the molecular and molar translational partition functions of $\text{X}_2$, respectively, then $\ln(Q_{t,m}) =$
($N$ is the Avogadro number)
questions.explanationEn:
For 1 mole ($N$ indistinguishable gas molecules of $\text{X}_2$), the molar translational partition function $Q_{t,m}$ is related to the molecular translational partition function $q_t$ by:
$Q_{t,m} = \frac{q_t^N}{N!}$.
Taking the natural logarithm and applying Stirling's approximation ($\ln(N!) \approx N\ln N - N$):
$\ln(Q_{t,m}) = N\ln q_t - \ln(N!) = N\ln q_t - (N\ln N - N) = N\ln q_t - N\ln N + N$.
Therefore, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Among the following, the NMR active nucleus(nuclei) is (are)
questions.explanationEn:
A nucleus is NMR active if and only if its nuclear spin quantum number $I \neq 0$:
- (A) $^{12}\text{C}$: even number of protons (6) and even number of neutrons (6) $\implies I = 0$ (NMR inactive).
- (B) $^{19}\text{F}$: odd mass number (9 protons, 10 neutrons) $\implies I = \frac{1}{2}$ (NMR active).
- (C) $^{2}\text{H}$ (deuterium): odd protons (1) and odd neutrons (1) $\implies I = 1$ (NMR active).
- (D) $^{16}\text{O}$: even protons (8) and even neutrons (8) $\implies I = 0$ (NMR inactive).
Hence, options (B) and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The complex(es) that exhibit(s) optical isomerism is (are)
questions.explanationEn:
An octahedral complex exhibits optical isomerism (exists as non-superimposable $\Delta$ and $\Lambda$ enantiomers) if it lacks improper symmetry elements ($\sigma$, $i$, $S_n$):
- (A) $[\text{Fe}(\text{acac})_3]$: tris-chelate $[\text{M}(\text{AA})_3]$ belongs to the chiral $D_3$ point group $\implies$ optically active.
- (B) $\textit{cis}\text{-}[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$: belongs to the chiral $C_2$ point group $\implies$ optically active.
- (C) $\textit{trans}\text{-}[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$: has a horizontal mirror plane ($\sigma_h$) and inversion center ($i$) ($D_{2h}$ symmetry) $\implies$ achiral / optically inactive.
- (D) $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$: tris-chelate $[\text{M}(\text{AA})_3]$ belongs to the chiral $D_3$ point group $\implies$ optically active.
Hence, options (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In aqueous solution of $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$, the allowed transition(s) is (are)
questions.explanationEn:
In $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$, iron is in the $+2$ oxidation state ($\text{Fe}^{2+}$, $3d^6$). Because $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong-field ligand, the octahedral complex $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$ is **low-spin** with ground-state configuration $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$ and ground-state term symbol **$^1A_{1g}$** (ruling out options A and D, which originate from the high-spin $^5T_{2g}$ state).
Promoting one electron from $t_{2g}$ to $e_g$ gives the excited configuration $t_{2g}^5 e_g^1$, which produces two spin-allowed ($\Delta S = 0$) singlet excited states: **$^1T_{1g}$** and **$^1T_{2g}$** (via $T_{2g} \otimes E_g = T_{1g} + T_{2g}$). Both spin-allowed transitions, $^1A_{1g} \to {^1T}_{1g}$ and $^1A_{1g} \to {^1T}_{2g}$, are observed in the electronic spectrum (becoming weakly vibronically allowed). Thus, options (B) and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The correct option(s) that give(s) **P** as the major product is (are), where **P** is methyl $(E)$-3-(4-isopropylcyclohex-1-en-1-yl)acrylate (an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated methyl ester conjugated to the double bond of 4-isopropylcyclohex-1-ene). [Diagram required - Q.51]
optionsEn: 4-Isopropylcyclohexan-1-one treated with 1. $\text{LDA}$, $\text{THF}$, $-78\ ^\circ\text{C}$, $\text{Tf}_2\text{O}$; 2. Methyl acrylate, $\text{Pd}(\text{PPh}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2$ ($2\text{ mol}\%$), $\text{Et}_3\text{N}$ ($3\text{ equiv.}$), $\text{DMF}$
questions.explanationEn:
Evaluate each synthetic route starting from 4-isopropylcyclohexan-1-one:
- (A) **Correct**: Step 1 converts the ketone into its enol triflate (4-isopropylcyclohex-1-en-1-yl triflate). Step 2 is a Pd-catalyzed **Heck coupling** with methyl acrylate, selectively forming the $(E)$-conjugated dienoate **P**.
- (B) **Correct**: Step 1–2 is a **Shapiro reaction** (tosylhydrazone + 2 equiv. $\text{MeLi}$ generates the vinyllithium intermediate, trapped with $\text{DMF}$ to give 4-isopropylcyclohex-1-ene-1-carbaldehyde). Step 3 is a **Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons (HWE)** olefination with trimethyl phosphonoacetate and $\text{NaH}$, giving the $(E)$-alkene **P**.
- (C) **Incorrect**: $\text{Me}_3\text{SiCH(Li)Cl}$ followed by $\text{HClO}_4$ converts the ketone into a saturated homologated aldehyde (4-isopropylcyclohexanecarbaldehyde); Reformatsky reaction ($\text{Zn}$, $\text{BrCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Me}$) and dehydration then yield methyl $(E)$-3-(4-isopropylcyclohexyl)acrylate (missing the endocyclic cyclohexene double bond).
- (D) **Incorrect**: Reduction to the alcohol, mesylation, $\text{NaCN}$ displacement, $\text{DIBAL-H}$ reduction to the saturated aldehyde, and Wittig olefination also give the saturated cyclohexane derivative, lacking the endocyclic double bond.
Hence, options (A) and (B) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
The correct statement(s) regarding **P**, **Q**, **R**, and **S** is (are):
- **P**: *cis*-1-bromo-4-*tert*-butylcyclohexane (both $^t\text{Bu}$ and $\text{Br}$ on bold wedges $\implies$ $\text{Br}$ is **axial**)
- **Q**: *trans*-1-bromo-4-*tert*-butylcyclohexane ($^t\text{Bu}$ wedged, $\text{Br}$ dashed $\implies$ $\text{Br}$ is **equatorial**)
- **R**: *cis*-4-*tert*-butylcyclohexan-1-ol (both $^t\text{Bu}$ and $\text{OH}$ on bold wedges $\implies$ $\text{OH}$ is **axial**)
- **S**: *trans*-4-*tert*-butylcyclohexan-1-ol ($^t\text{Bu}$ wedged, $\text{OH}$ dashed $\implies$ $\text{OH}$ is **equatorial**) [Diagram required - Q.52]
optionsEn: **P** reacts faster than **Q** with $\text{PhSNa}$ in $\text{DMF}$ as a solvent.
**Q** reacts faster than **P** with $\text{NaN}_3$ in $\text{DMF}$ as a solvent.
**R** reacts faster than **S** when treated with $\text{TsCl}/\text{Et}_3\text{N}$ in $\text{DCM}$ as a solvent.
**R** gets oxidized faster than **S** when reacted with $\text{CrO}_3$ in $\text{DCM}$ as a solvent.
questions.explanationEn:
The bulky 4-*tert*-butyl group locks the cyclohexane ring with $^t\text{Bu}$ equatorial. Thus, the *cis*-isomers (**P**, **R**) have axial substituents ($\text{Br}$, $\text{OH}$), whereas the *trans*-isomers (**Q**, **S**) have equatorial substituents:
- (A) **Correct**: In $S_N2$ substitution with $\text{PhSNa}$ in polar aprotic $\text{DMF}$, the axial bromide **P** reacts faster than the equatorial bromide **Q** because (i) **P** has higher ground-state energy due to 1,3-diaxial steric strain, and (ii) backside equatorial attack on **P** is sterically less hindered than backside axial attack on **Q**.
- (B) **Incorrect**: By the exact same $S_N2$ principle with $\text{NaN}_3$ in $\text{DMF}$, axial **P** reacts faster than equatorial **Q**.
- (C) **Incorrect**: Esterification/tosylation with $\text{TsCl}/\text{Et}_3\text{N}$ occurs at the hydroxyl oxygen; the less sterically hindered equatorial alcohol **S** reacts faster than the sterically crowded axial alcohol **R**.
- (D) **Correct**: In chromic acid ($\text{CrO}_3$) oxidation of cyclohexanols, the rate-determining step is removal of the $\text{C-H}$ proton from the chromate ester, which relieves the severe 1,3-diaxial steric crowding in the axial alcohol **R**. Hence, axial **R** oxidizes faster than equatorial **S**.
Therefore, options (A) and (D) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
1,2-Dimethylenecyclohexane $\xrightarrow{\mathbf{L},\ \text{benzene},\ 25\ ^\circ\text{C}}$ **M**.
Path 1: **M** $\xrightarrow{\text{1. }\mathbf{N};\ \text{2. Pd-C, H}_2}$ *cis*-decalin.
Path 2: **M** $\xrightarrow{\text{1. }\mathbf{X},\ \text{EtBr};\ \text{2. }\mathbf{N};\ \text{3. Pd-C, H}_2}$ **O**.
The correct option(s) is (are) [Diagram required - Q.53]
questions.explanationEn:
Analyze the Diels-Alder / sulfone alkylation-desulfonylation sequence:
- **L** is (vinylsulfonyl)benzene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH-SO}_2\text{Ph}$), an ethylene equivalent dienophile. Its [4+2] Diels-Alder cycloaddition with 1,2-dimethylenecyclohexane in benzene at $25\ ^\circ\text{C}$ yields the bicyclic sulfone **M**, 2-(phenylsulfonyl)-1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8-octahydronaphthalene.
- In Path 1, reductive desulfonylation of **M** using **N** = $\text{Na-Hg}/\text{MeOH}$ removes the $-\text{SO}_2\text{Ph}$ group to give $\Delta^{9,10}$-octalin, and subsequent syn-hydrogenation ($\text{Pd-C},\ \text{H}_2$) yields *cis*-decalin. Thus **(A) is correct**.
- In Path 2, deprotonation of the acidic $\alpha$-sulfonyl proton of **M** with a strong non-nucleophilic base **X** = $\text{LDA}$ followed by alkylation with $\text{EtBr}$ introduces an ethyl group at C2. Subsequent desulfonylation with $\text{Na-Hg}/\text{MeOH}$ (**N**) and hydrogenation ($\text{Pd-C},\ \text{H}_2$) produces 2-ethyldecalin (**O**). Thus **(B) is correct**.
- (C) is incorrect because acrolein would give an aldehyde rather than a sulfone removable to *cis*-decalin, and (D) is incorrect because $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is a reducing agent, not a base for $\alpha$-alkylation with $\text{EtBr}$.
Hence, options (A) and (B) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following reaction sequence where **M** and **N** are the major products:
Starting material: diethyl *trans*-bicyclo[2.2.0]hex-5-ene-2,3-dicarboxylate (cis-fused cyclobutene-cyclobutane with both bridgehead H's wedged; one $-\text{CO}_2\text{Et}$ dashed, the other $-\text{CO}_2\text{Et}$ wedged).
Reaction: Starting material $\xrightarrow{\text{Cl}_2(\text{PCy}_3)_2\text{Ru=CH-Ph (2 mol\%)},\ \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2}$ **M** $\xrightarrow{190\ ^\circ\text{C}}$ **N**.
The correct option(s) is (are) [Diagram required - Q.54]
optionsEn: **M** = diethyl *trans*-3,4-divinylcyclobutane-1,2-dicarboxylate (both vinyl groups cis/dashed, bridgehead H's wedged, two $-\text{CO}_2\text{Et}$ groups trans)
questions.explanationEn:
Step 1 is a **ring-opening cross-metathesis (ROCM)** catalyzed by Grubbs first-generation catalyst ($\text{Cl}_2(\text{PCy}_3)_2\text{Ru=CH-Ph}$) in the presence of ethylene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$). The strained cyclobutene ring opens selectively by metathesis with ethylene to install two cis-oriented vinyl groups on the remaining cyclobutane ring, forming **M** = diethyl *trans*-3,4-divinylcyclobutane-1,2-dicarboxylate (option A is correct; option B is simple hydrogenation, which does not occur).
Step 2: Heating the *cis*-1,2-divinylcyclobutane **M** at $190\ ^\circ\text{C}$ induces a facile thermal **[3,3]-sigmatropic Cope rearrangement** driven by the release of cyclobutane ring strain, expanding the 4-membered ring into an 8-membered ring to yield **N** = diethyl *trans*-cycloocta-1,5-diene-3,4-dicarboxylate (option C is correct; option D is wrong).
Therefore, options (A) and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
The correct statement(s) about the relationship for the $\text{H}$-atoms in the following compounds is (are):
- Left compound: norbornane (bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane) with C2 bearing *endo*-$\text{H}_1$ and *exo*-$\text{H}_2$, and C3 bearing *endo*-$\text{H}_3$ and *exo*-$\text{H}_4$.
- Right compound: bicyclo[2.2.2]octane with C2 bearing down-$\text{H}_5$ and up-$\text{H}_6$, and C3 bearing down-$\text{H}_7$ and up-$\text{H}_8$. [Diagram required - Q.55]
optionsEn: $\text{H}_1$ and $\text{H}_3$ are enantiotopic; $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{H}_3$ are diastereotopic.
$\text{H}_1$ and $\text{H}_3$ are diastereotopic; $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{H}_3$ are enantiotopic.
$\text{H}_5$ and $\text{H}_7$ are enantiotopic; $\text{H}_6$ and $\text{H}_7$ are homotopic.
$\text{H}_5$ and $\text{H}_7$ are homotopic; $\text{H}_6$ and $\text{H}_7$ are enantiotopic.
questions.explanationEn:
Use symmetry criteria (homotopic = interchangeable by a $C_n$ proper rotation; enantiotopic = interchangeable only by an improper operation such as $\sigma$, $i$, or $S_n$; diastereotopic = not interchangeable by any symmetry operation):
1. **Norbornane** ($C_{2v}$ symmetry): A vertical mirror plane ($\sigma_v$) passes through the C7 bridge and bisects the C2-C3 bond, reflecting *endo*-$\text{H}_1$ into *endo*-$\text{H}_3$. No proper $C_n$ axis exchanges C2 and C3 (the $C_2$ axis passes through C7 and exchanges C2-C3 with C5-C6). Therefore, $\text{H}_1$ and $\text{H}_3$ are **enantiotopic**. Meanwhile, $\text{H}_2$ (*exo*) and $\text{H}_3$ (*endo*) occupy chemically non-equivalent environments and are **diastereotopic**. Thus **(A) is correct**.
2. **Bicyclo[2.2.2]octane** ($D_{3h}$ symmetry): A horizontal mirror plane ($\sigma_h$) bisects all three $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2-$ bridges, reflecting down-$\text{H}_5$ into down-$\text{H}_7$, while no $C_n$ axis maps $\text{H}_5$ to $\text{H}_7$; hence $\text{H}_5$ and $\text{H}_7$ are **enantiotopic**. A $C_2$ axis perpendicular to the principal $C_3$ axis passes through the midpoint of the C2-C3 bond, rotating up-$\text{H}_6$ directly into down-$\text{H}_7$; hence $\text{H}_6$ and $\text{H}_7$ are **homotopic**. Thus **(C) is correct**.
Therefore, options (A) and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Among the following, the correct statement(s) is (are):
optionsEn: the normalization factor of a Slater determinant for a 3-electron atom is $\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}}$.
the number of nodes in the radial wave function of $3s$ orbital of a hydrogen atom is the same as the number of nodes in the angular wave function of a $4d$ orbital of hydrogen atom.
the energy separation between any two adjacent states is same for a harmonic oscillator, while it is different for a rigid rotor.
the magnitude of the total spin angular momentum of an $\alpha$ electron is the negative of that of a $\beta$ electron.
questions.explanationEn:
Check each quantum-mechanical statement:
- (A) **Incorrect**: For an $N$-electron system, the normalization factor of a Slater determinant is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{N!}}$. For $N = 3$, it is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3!}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$, not $\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}}$.
- (B) **Correct**: The number of radial nodes is $n - l - 1$, so for a $3s$ orbital ($n=3, l=0$) it is $3 - 0 - 1 = 2$. The number of angular nodes is $l$, so for a $4d$ orbital ($n=4, l=2$) it is $2$. Both equal $2$.
- (C) **Correct**: For a harmonic oscillator, $E_v = (v + \frac{1}{2})h\nu$, so $\Delta E = E_{v+1} - E_v = h\nu$ (constant). For a rigid rotor, $E_J = BJ(J+1)$, so $\Delta E = E_{J+1} - E_J = 2B(J+1)$, which increases with $J$.
- (D) **Incorrect**: The magnitude of total spin angular momentum is $\sqrt{s(s+1)}\hbar = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\hbar$, which is always positive and identical for both $\alpha$ ($m_s = +1/2$) and $\beta$ ($m_s = -1/2$) electrons (only their $z$-components $S_z = \pm \frac{1}{2}\hbar$ have opposite signs).
Hence, options (B) and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Among the following, the correct statement(s) is (are):
optionsEn: $C_2$ symmetry element is present in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ but NOT in $\text{PCl}_5$.
both $C_2$ and $C_3$ symmetry elements are present in $\text{CCl}_4$ and $\text{SF}_6$.
one $\sigma_h$ and three $\sigma_d$ symmetry elements are present in benzene.
$\sigma_v$ symmetry element is present in $\text{NH}_3$ but NOT in $\text{BF}_3$.
questions.explanationEn:
Evaluate the point group symmetry elements of each molecule:
- (A) **Incorrect**: $\text{PCl}_5$ (trigonal bipyramidal, $D_{3h}$) possesses **three $C_2$ axes** perpendicular to the principal $C_3$ axis (each passing through the central $\text{P}$ and one equatorial $\text{Cl}$), in addition to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($C_{2v}$) and $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ ($C_2$).
- (B) **Correct**: $\text{CCl}_4$ ($T_d$) has three $C_2$ axes and four $C_3$ axes; $\text{SF}_6$ ($O_h$) has nine $C_2$ axes (three collinear with $C_4$ and six $C_2'$) and four $C_3$ axes. Both contain $C_2$ and $C_3$.
- (C) **Correct**: Benzene ($D_{6h}$) possesses one horizontal mirror plane ($\sigma_h$, the molecular plane), three $\sigma_v$ planes (passing through opposite $\text{C-H}$ bonds), and **three $\sigma_d$ planes** (bisecting opposite $\text{C-C}$ bonds).
- (D) **Incorrect**: Both $\text{NH}_3$ ($C_{3v}$) and $\text{BF}_3$ ($D_{3h}$) possess three $\sigma_v$ mirror planes.
Hence, options (B) and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
$\Delta S^\circ$ (in $\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$) for the given reaction at $298\text{ K}$ is ________.
$[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+} + \text{en} \rightleftharpoons [\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4(\text{en})]^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$
(Given: $\log K_1 = 10.6$, where $K_1$ is the equilibrium constant. $\Delta H^\circ = -54\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $R = 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$)
(rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn:
First calculate the standard Gibbs free energy change $\Delta G^\circ$ at $T = 298\text{ K}$:
$\Delta G^\circ = -2.303 RT \log K_1 = -2.302585 \times 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1} \times 298\text{ K} \times 10.6 = -60471.0\text{ J mol}^{-1}$ (using $2.303$ gives $-60481.9\text{ J mol}^{-1}$).
Now apply $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$ with $\Delta H^\circ = -54000\text{ J mol}^{-1}$:
$\Delta S^\circ = \frac{\Delta H^\circ - \Delta G^\circ}{T} = \frac{-54000 - (-60471.0)}{298} = \frac{6471.0}{298} = 21.71\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$ (or $21.75\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$ with $2.303$; the positive $\Delta S^\circ$ reflects the chelate effect as 2 particles form 3). This falls squarely within the official answer range $21.40\text{ to }22.00$.

questions.questionTextEn:
The turnover frequency (in $\text{h}^{-1}$) of a reaction where $5\text{ mol}\%$ of a catalyst is required for $90\%$ conversion in $3\text{ h}$ is ____.
(rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanationEn:
The turnover number ($\text{TON}$) is the number of moles of substrate converted to product per mole of catalyst:
$\text{TON} = \frac{\text{moles of product}}{\text{moles of catalyst}} = \frac{90\%}{5\%} = \frac{0.90}{0.05} = 18$.
The turnover frequency ($\text{TOF}$) is the turnover number per unit time:
$\text{TOF} = \frac{\text{TON}}{t} = \frac{18}{3\text{ h}} = 6\text{ h}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
In thermogravimetric analysis, $12.45\text{ mg}$ of $\text{CuSO}_4\cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$ was subjected to heating under $\text{N}_2$ atmosphere. At a particular temperature, there was a weight loss of $3.6\text{ mg}$. The number of water molecule(s) lost per formula unit is ____.
(Given molar mass (in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$) of $\text{H} = 1.0$, $\text{O} = 16.0$, $\text{S} = 32.0$, and $\text{Cu} = 63.5$)
(rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanationEn:
Calculate the molar mass of $\text{CuSO}_4\cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$:
$M(\text{CuSO}_4\cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}) = 63.5 + 32.0 + 4(16.0) + 5(18.0) = 159.5 + 90.0 = 249.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
Number of millimoles of $\text{CuSO}_4\cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$ taken:
$n_{\text{salt}} = \frac{12.45\text{ mg}}{249.5\text{ mg mmol}^{-1}} = 0.04990\text{ mmol} \approx 0.050\text{ mmol}$.
Number of millimoles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($M = 18.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) lost:
$n_{\text{H}_2\text{O}} = \frac{3.6\text{ mg}}{18.0\text{ mg mmol}^{-1}} = 0.200\text{ mmol}$.
Number of water molecules lost per formula unit $= \frac{0.200}{0.04990} = 4.008 \approx 4$.

questions.questionTextEn:
In the given reaction sequence, the amount of **R** produced (in $\text{g}$) is ____.
Reaction sequence: Benzene ($7.8\text{ g}$) $\xrightarrow{\text{oleum (excess), }200\ ^\circ\text{C}\ (80\%)}$ **P** $\xrightarrow{\text{NaOH, heat; then H}_3\text{O}^+\ (75\%)}$ **Q** $\xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_3\text{ (excess)}/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{ (excess)}\ (50\%)}$ **R**.
(Given: molar mass (in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$) of $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{N} = 14$, $\text{O} = 16$, and $\text{S} = 32$)
(rounded off to two decimal places) [Diagram required - Q.61]
questions.explanationEn:
Trace the structure and molar yield at each step:
1. Initial moles of benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$, $M = 78\text{ g mol}^{-1}$): $n_0 = \frac{7.8}{78} = 0.10\text{ mol}$.
2. Exhaustive sulfonation with excess oleum at $200\ ^\circ\text{C}$ yields **benzene-1,3-disulfonic acid** (**P**; meta-disubstitution) in $80\%$ yield: $n_P = 0.10 \times 0.80 = 0.080\text{ mol}$.
3. Alkali fusion ($\text{NaOH}$, heat) followed by acidification converts both $-\text{SO}_3\text{H}$ groups to $-\text{OH}$, giving **resorcinol** (benzene-1,3-diol, **Q**) in $75\%$ yield: $n_Q = 0.080 \times 0.75 = 0.060\text{ mol}$.
4. Nitration of strongly activated resorcinol with excess $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ yields **2,4,6-trinitroresorcinol** (styphnic acid, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_3\text{N}_3\text{O}_8$, **R**) in $50\%$ yield: $n_R = 0.060 \times 0.50 = 0.030\text{ mol}$.
Molar mass of **R** ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_3\text{N}_3\text{O}_8$): $6(12) + 3(1) + 3(14) + 8(16) = 72 + 3 + 42 + 128 = 245\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
Mass of **R** produced $= 0.030\text{ mol} \times 245\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 7.35\text{ g}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
The wave function of a particle in a cubic box (of side $L$) is given by
$\psi(x, y, z) = \sqrt{32/L^3}\sin\frac{\pi x}{L}\cos\frac{\pi x}{L}\sin\frac{2\pi y}{L}\sin\frac{\pi z}{L}$.
The ratio of the energy of the state corresponding to the above wave function to the ground state energy is ____.
(rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanationEn:
Use the trigonometric identity $2\sin\theta\cos\theta = \sin(2\theta)$ to rewrite the $x$-dependent factor:
$\sin\frac{\pi x}{L}\cos\frac{\pi x}{L} = \frac{1}{2}\sin\frac{2\pi x}{L}$.
Substituting this into $\psi(x, y, z)$ gives:
$\psi(x, y, z) = \sqrt{\frac{32}{L^3}} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\sin\frac{2\pi x}{L}\sin\frac{2\pi y}{L}\sin\frac{\pi z}{L} = \sqrt{\frac{8}{L^3}}\sin\frac{2\pi x}{L}\sin\frac{2\pi y}{L}\sin\frac{\pi z}{L}$.
This is the normalized eigenfunction of a 3D cubic box with quantum numbers $(n_x, n_y, n_z) = (2, 2, 1)$. Since $E_{n_x, n_y, n_z} = \frac{h^2}{8mL^2}(n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2)$ and the ground state has $(1, 1, 1)$:
$\frac{E_{2,2,1}}{E_{1,1,1}} = \frac{2^2 + 2^2 + 1^2}{1^2 + 1^2 + 1^2} = \frac{9}{3} = 3$.

questions.questionTextEn:
$\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ are normalized eigenfunctions of a Hermitian operator.
$|\psi\rangle = 3i|\phi_1\rangle + 2|\phi_2\rangle$ and $|\chi\rangle = -2i|\phi_1\rangle + 5|\phi_2\rangle$.
The value of $\langle\psi|\chi\rangle + \langle\chi|\psi\rangle$ is ____.
(rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanationEn:
Since $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ are normalized eigenfunctions of a Hermitian operator (corresponding to distinct eigenvalues, hence orthonormal: $\langle\phi_1|\phi_1\rangle = \langle\phi_2|\phi_2\rangle = 1$ and $\langle\phi_1|\phi_2\rangle = \langle\phi_2|\phi_1\rangle = 0$), take the complex conjugate for the bra vector $\langle\psi| = -3i\langle\phi_1| + 2\langle\phi_2|$:
$\langle\psi|\chi\rangle = (-3i)(-2i)\langle\phi_1|\phi_1\rangle + (2)(5)\langle\phi_2|\phi_2\rangle = 6i^2 + 10 = -6 + 10 = 4$.
By the Hermitian property of inner products, $\langle\chi|\psi\rangle = \langle\psi|\chi\rangle^* = 4^* = 4$.
Therefore, $\langle\psi|\chi\rangle + \langle\chi|\psi\rangle = 4 + 4 = 8$.

questions.questionTextEn:
$2\text{ mol}$ of a monoatomic ideal gas with initial volume of $5\text{ L}$ and pressure $10\text{ bar}$ undergoes an irreversible adiabatic expansion against a constant final pressure of $1\text{ bar}$. The final volume (in $\text{L}$) is ______.
(Given: $R = 8.314 \times 10^{-2}\text{ L bar mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$)
(rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.explanationEn:
For an adiabatic process ($q = 0$), the first law gives $\Delta U = w$. For a monoatomic ideal gas, $C_{V,m} = \frac{3}{2}R$, and for irreversible expansion against a constant external pressure $P_{\text{ext}} = P_2 = 1\text{ bar}$:
$n C_{V,m}(T_2 - T_1) = -P_2(V_2 - V_1)$.
Substituting $nRT_1 = P_1 V_1$ and $nRT_2 = P_2 V_2$:
$\frac{3}{2}(P_2 V_2 - P_1 V_1) = -P_2(V_2 - V_1) \implies \frac{5}{2} P_2 V_2 = \frac{3}{2} P_1 V_1 + P_2 V_1$.
Plugging in $P_1 = 10\text{ bar}$, $V_1 = 5\text{ L}$, and $P_2 = 1\text{ bar}$:
$2.5(1) V_2 = 1.5(10)(5) + (1)(5) = 75 + 5 = 80 \implies V_2 = \frac{80}{2.5} = 32.0\text{ L}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
The following figure shows an experimental liquid-liquid phase diagram of phenol and water at the vapor pressure of the system (Temperature in $^\circ\text{C}$ vs. mole fraction of phenol, with upper critical solution temperature $\approx 72\ ^\circ\text{C}$ at $x_{\text{phenol}} \approx 0.30$; at $40\ ^\circ\text{C}$, the coexistence curve gives $x_{\text{phenol}} \approx 0.10$ for the water-rich phase and $x_{\text{phenol}} \approx 0.60$ for the phenol-rich phase). The total amount of phenol and water (in $\text{mol}$) present in the phenol-rich phase when $5\text{ mol}$ of water was shaken with $5\text{ mol}$ of phenol at $40\ ^\circ\text{C}$ is ______.
(rounded off to one decimal place) [Diagram required - Q.65]
questions.explanationEn:
Mixing $5\text{ mol}$ of water and $5\text{ mol}$ of phenol gives a total amount $n_{\text{total}} = 10\text{ mol}$ with overall phenol mole fraction $x_{\text{overall}} = \frac{5}{5 + 5} = 0.50$.
Reading the horizontal tie-line at $T = 40\ ^\circ\text{C}$ from the liquid-liquid coexistence curve:
- Water-rich phase composition: $x_1 \approx 0.10$
- Phenol-rich phase composition: $x_2 \approx 0.60$
Applying the **lever rule**, the fraction of total moles in the phenol-rich phase is:
$\frac{n_{\text{phenol-rich}}}{n_{\text{total}}} = \frac{x_{\text{overall}} - x_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{0.50 - 0.10}{0.60 - 0.10} = \frac{0.40}{0.50} = 0.80$.
Therefore, the total amount of phenol and water in the phenol-rich phase is:
$n_{\text{phenol-rich}} = 0.80 \times 10\text{ mol} = 8.0\text{ mol}$ (within the official range $7.8\text{ to }8.2$).
